title: Request: contingent capacity top-up & amortized surcharge smoothing for Q3 launch
text:
Request: contingent capacity top-up & amortized surcharge smoothing for Q3 launch

["From: Ethan Cross <ethan.cross@brightlane.com>\\nTo: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>\\nDate: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700\\nSubject: Request: contingent capacity top-up & amortized surcharge smoothing for Q3 launch\\n\\nHi Jonas —\\n\\nWe've been load-testing the integration and expect a concentrated traffic spike during our Q3 feature rollout (projected 72-hour window). We love Redwood's performance but are worried about short-window overrun costs blowing out our budget.\\n\\nTwo asks: can you provide a short-term top-up path that avoids punitive per-token surcharges, and can the extra consumption be amortized across the next two invoices (rather than billed as a one-time overrun)?\\n\\nWe have a Managed Procurement window next week and need a written proposal to review with finance. Happy to jump on a quick call.\\n\\nThanks,\\nEthan\\nEthan Cross\\nHead of Integrations — BrightLane\\n\\n---\\nAttachments: none\\n", "From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>\\nTo: Ethan Cross <ethan.cross@brightlane.com>\\nCc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>\\nDate: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Request: contingent capacity top-up & amortized surcharge smoothing for Q3 launch\\n\\nEthan —\\n\\nAppreciate the heads up. Short answer: yes, we can offer a contingent bulk-topup with an amortized surcharge option. To make it actionable for your procurement team we usually: \\n\\n- Define a temporary uplift band (e.g., +40% throughput for a 72-hour window)\\n- Cap the effective per-token surcharge inside that band at a negotiated blended rate\\n- Convert the consumed uplift into a staged true-up split across the next 2 invoices (or applied as a credit against the following quarter)\\n\\nA few clarifying Qs so we can draft formal terms:\\n1) Do you need the uplift to be pre-paid (credit) or invoice-then-amortize?\\n2) Is the spike predictable in UTC window(s or rolling)?\\n3) Any compliance/approval constraints from procurement/legal we should loop in now?\\n\\nI'll work with Pricing and Legal on a concrete term sheet. Looping Karthik + Naomi to propose pricing and accounting flows.\\n\\nBest,\\nJonas Weber\\nDirector, GTM — Redwood Inference\\n\\n---\\n", 'From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>\\nTo: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ethan Cross <ethan.cross@brightlane.com>\\nCc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>\\nDate: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:20:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Request: contingent capacity top-up & amortized surcharge smoothing for Q3 launch\\n\\nEthan / team —\\n\\nThanks for the detail. We\'ve sketched three practical options (summary below) — I\'ll attach a short term-sheet with the preferred recommendation.\\n\\nOption A — Provisional Top-up (no prepay):\\n- Temporary uplift band: +40% baseline for 72 hours\\n- Blended uplift rate: USD 0.0125 per extra token (capped)\\n- Billing: uplift consumption invoiced; buyer elects amortization over 2 invoices (equal installments)\\n- Eligibility: requires PO or written confirmation before start window\\n\\nOption B — Escrowed Credit (preferred for tight budgets):\\n- Customer prepays an escrow credit (estimate) at a 10% discount to uplift list rates\\n- If not fully consumed, remaining credit rolls into next month\\n- If consumption exceeds escrow, overrun billed at blended uplift rate with amortization\\n\\nOption C — Contingent Amnesty (one-time concession):\\n- For strategic pilots we can offer a partial surcharge waiver up to a threshold, with the excess amortized\\n\\nRecommendation: Option B for BrightLane — gives predictable cashflow for finance and avoids a surprise one-time hit. Attached: \\"proposed-amnesty-terms.pdf\\" (term language + sample invoice flow) and a simple billing diagram (billing-workflow-diagram.png).\\n\\nIf procurement prefers invoice-first, we can flip A but will need a nominal administrative surcharge (0.5% of uplift invoice) to cover amortization handling.\\n\\nHappy to jump on a 20-min call to finalize numbers.\\n\\nThanks,\\nKarthik Iyer\\nHead of Pricing & Growth — Redwood Inference\\n\\n---\\nAttachments: proposed-amnesty-terms.pdf, billing-workflow-diagram.png\\n', "From: Ethan Cross <ethan.cross@brightlane.com>\\nTo: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>\\nCc: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@clearpay.com>\\nDate: Wed, 26 May 2027 07:48:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Request: contingent capacity top-up & amortized surcharge smoothing for Q3 launch\\n\\nKarthik / Jonas —\\n\\nThanks for the quick options. Procurement liked Option B but wants clarity on two items before we sign off:\\n1) If we prepay and don't use the full credit, is the residual refundable or auto-applied to next quarter? (BrightLane finance prefers refund, legal prefers carry-forward)\\n2) Can you confirm the amortization entries: will Redwood produce a single uplift invoice and then two amortization credit notes, or will it be split into two invoices from the outset? Our AP system is rigid — we need the expected invoice artifact.\\n\\nAlso, small ask: can we get a one-line carve-out in the terms that prevents automatic renewal of the escrow credit? We need explicit renewal consent.\\n\\nIf you can send a redlined term-sheet with those clarifications, I can fast-track procurement review.\\n\\nBest,\\nEthan\\n\\n---\\n", "From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>\\nTo: Ethan Cross <ethan.cross@brightlane.com>\\nCc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>\\nDate: Thu, 27 May 2027 16:45:00 -07:00\\nSubject: Re: Request: contingent capacity top-up & amortized surcharge smoothing for Q3 launch\\n\\nEthan —\\n\\nGood questions. Short answers and next steps below: \\n\\n1) Residual credit handling: we can offer either (a) refund within 30 days post-window or (b) carry-forward to the next billing quarter. We'll put both as toggles on the term sheet and leave the checkbox to BrightLane.\\n\\n2) Invoice artifacts: Redwood will issue a single uplift invoice post-window that records total uplift consumption. If you elect amortization, we will generate two subsequent credit invoices (amortization schedule) that your AP can reconcile. If you need the uplift split into two invoices up-front, we can accommodate but it will add an administrative processing fee of USD 200 per split.\\n\\n3) Renewal carve-out: confirmed — escrow credits will be explicit opt-in and will not auto-renew unless both parties sign an extension. We'll add the one-line carve-out.\\n\\nNext steps: Karthik and Naomi will produce a redline-ready term-sheet (we've attached the draft). I'll share a DocuSign link for signature and loop in Legal if the doc requires additional clauses.\\n\\nProposed call: Fri 28 May, 9:00am PT — 20 minutes to finalize. Let me know if that works and I'll calendar invite.\\n\\nThanks,\\nJonas Weber\\nDirector, GTM — Redwood Inference\\n\\n---\\nAttachments included: proposed-amnesty-terms.pdf, billing-workflow-diagram.png\\n"]
